title: Today That You Have Returned, We Both Were Silent
text:
Today that you have returned, we both were silent,

and only our old thoughts

lit the sweet darkness

of being together and saying nothing.


Only our hands clasped so tightly

as if breaking the iron of absence.

If only a cloud would eclipse our lives!


Leave in my heart the new voices,

the very clear, present assault

of your person upon the landscapes

that are in me for the air of your life.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the reunited silence and hands breaking the iron of absence.

title: The Sower Sowed the Dawn...
text:
The sower sowed the dawn;

his arm encompassed the sea.

Into his gaze the mountains

could enter.


The furrow-scored earth

heard the grains fall.

From that simple and deep rhythm

melodically the trees set their dance swaying.


Silent sower:

the sun has grown through your magic hands.

The field has chosen another tone

and the sky has flown higher.


He sowed the earth.

His step was beautiful: neither short nor long.

In his eyes the mountains fit.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sower's cosmic scale and the rhythm of grains, trees, and dawn.

title: The Reaper, with Pauses of Music...
text:
The reaper, with pauses of music,

was reaping the afternoon.

His sickle is so fine

that it reaps the sweet ears and reaps the afternoon.


Reaper who walks on golden levels

with his sharpened sound,

defeating the fine heights of gold,

he also brings down the sunset.


He reaped the clear ears.

His pause was music.

His shadow lengthened the afternoon.

In his eyes he brought a morning star

that sometimes leaped over the whole landscape.


The sickle, sharpened so finely,

reaped the same:

the ear of grain and the last sun of afternoon.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the reaper's sickle cutting both grain and sunset.

title: I Caress the Landscape...
text:
I caress the landscape,

oh adored person

who heard my poems and who now

rests your head on my arm.


(...) Behind a large hill

a cloud is slowly bursting.

its surprise

is like our happiness: so first!

The inaugural, which in our love is the key

to every fullness.

The air trembles at our feet. I have

your head on my chest. everything curdles

the enormous transparency of a silence,

panoramic, smooth,

supported by the pale delirium

of kissing your cheeks in silence.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the intimate landscape and the panoramic silence of the beloved's head on the speaker's chest.

title: Ah, My Heart, Which No One Wanted...
text:
Ah, my heart, which no one wanted

to take between my desolate hands.

You came to look at its flames

and watched it burn clear and submissive.


(The deep foot upon the black floor

bled lights through all the days.

Before the geographic feet, silent,

your invisible doors, Paradise.)


You who threw another log onto the embers,

gather the ashes and the small

heart that moves you; join and leave it.


Someday you will sigh, some

night of solitude you will hear my complaint,

yours to the heart like no other.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the burned heart, Paradise doors, and future solitary complaint.

title: Poetry
text:
Poetry, truth, my poem,

force of love that found your hands, far away,

in a flight of Junes polished mirrors

and found in light paleness, cold.


I overflowed the river's pitchers,

stopped the light in the old backwaters,

gave orders to all reflections;

perfect June gave its power.


Poetry, truth of every dream,

never have I been a shorter owner of you

than in this master in whose clouds I die.


Flee from me, turn me into your oblivion,

into impossible time, into the first

of all memories of oblivion.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the address to poetry and the paradox of becoming memory inside oblivion.

title: The Time That Unites and Divides Us
text:
The time that unites and divides us

—nocturnal fruit tree and flowering day—

today beside you, tomorrow distance,

devours what it forgets and what it asks.


To care within it for what in flight it neglects

will be to enter its clockwork;

and minute by minute and day by day,

without wanting to, however little, it forgets us.


Forgotten by time, those instants

will be of eternity; the dazzling

moments of the instant of the eternal.


June in your hands refines its beauty;

autumn is its docile subordinate.

Your soul combines time and eternity.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Pellicer's time-eternity sonnet and the seasonal hierarchy around the beloved.

title: Nameless Love
text:
Nameless love, destined realm

of being and of not being there. Your sudden siege

sustains my pain and cancels the tedium

of exhausted cup or pressed wine.


In a high silence, an aquiline

blue span of silence, I live. In the midst

of the ill-fated patience of your siege

I open the cages and overflow the trill.


For you I hang crowns on the walls;

for you I am more fugitive and in ripe

dreamings I lighten your songs.


And I carry you in my being and you have gathered

the attitude that in Florences or Byzantiums

consecrates its doves to oblivion.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the nameless love as siege, silence, and consecration to oblivion.

title: The Mexican Flag
text:
The Mexican flag

—green, white, and red—

in its colors shelters

the Homeland in sovereign bloom.

When in our hands we hold

our flag,

it is like holding whole

water, ships, light, and oars.


When we raise its colors,

our heart feels

the joy of a song

that pours itself out in flowers.


For love of my flag,

I call everyone "brother."

Whoever carries it in hand

carries peace wherever he wishes.


Peace, work, love, and faith

are the sky of my flag.

I want, as all my longing,

to stand worthily at its foot.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the civic hymn tone and the flag as vessel of peace, work, love, and faith.

title: This Boat Without Oars Is Mine
text:
This boat without oars is mine.

To the wind, to the wind, to the wind alone

it has given its course, its indolent

desolation of sterile distance.


Everything has already lost its hierarchy.

I am full of nothing and beneath the bridge

only the mud, the ill-living

ruin of the water and its silverwork.


Everyone leaves or comes. I remain

for whatever losing courage and fear may give.

To the wind, to the wind, to whatever the wind wants!


A sea without honor and without piracy,

heights of any blue whatsoever,

and this boat without oars that is mine.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the oarless boat surrendered to wind and the speaker's remaining in loss.
